title: The secret handshake
prompt:
Two friends send each other a secret handshake as a number. Only the low five bits count:

- bit 0 (1): wave
- bit 1 (2): nod
- bit 2 (4): wink
- bit 3 (8): clap
- bit 4 (16): do the actions in reverse order

The starter reads the number into `code_r` and holds the five strings. Print the action for each set bit among bits 0 to 3, one per line, lowest bit first. When bit 4 is set, print them highest bit first instead. Bits above bit 4 mean nothing. When none of bits 0 to 3 is set, print `no handshake`.

`tst` works out the AND of two values and sets the flags from it without keeping the result, so `tst code_r, 4` then `b.ne` jumps when bit 2 is set. A mask (a value with only the bits you care about set) that walks through 1, 2, 4, 8, or 8, 4, 2, 1, lets one loop test every bit.

With the sample input `11` (binary `01011`) the output is:

```
wave
nod
clap
```

## What is checked

- the actions for the sample input, one per line
- the program exits cleanly
- the bits are tested with `tst`
- the same program gives the right handshake for other numbers, including 0, reversed codes, and a negative number
starter:
// decode the low five bits of a number into a secret handshake
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(code_r, w19)
define(mask_r, w20)
define(count_r, w21)

.data
fmt_code:   .string "%d"
act_wave:   .string "wave\n"
act_nod:    .string "nod\n"
act_wink:   .string "wink\n"
act_clap:   .string "clap\n"
msg_none:   .string "no handshake\n"

.bss
.balign 4
code_m:     .skip 4

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_code               // read the code into code_m
        ldr     x1, =code_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =code_m
        ldr     code_r, [x9]

        // TODO: for each of bits 0 to 3 that is set in code_r, print its
        // action (1 wave, 2 nod, 4 wink, 8 clap), lowest bit first. When
        // bit 4 (16) is set, print them highest bit first instead. When
        // none of bits 0 to 3 is set, print msg_none. printf may change
        // x0 to x18, so keep anything you need later in w19 to w28.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
